title: kt-null-graph-controls: code and run files for "Do log-built concept graphs help KC-level learner models? Entry-point null graphs, a positive control and decision-level tests"
description:
Code, run files and analysis scripts for the manuscript "Do log-built concept graphs help KC-level learner models? Entry-point null graphs, a positive control and decision-level tests" (H. B. Truong, under revision for User Modeling and User-Adapted Interaction).

The study fixes KC-level tracers and measures a concept graph against an empty-graph control that keeps every other parameter, a ladder of null graphs, fixed random codes, capacity controls and seed ensembles on ten public corpora, at four working entry points (embedding refinement, state channel, the training loss of PDKT and the propagation of GKT; a fifth, attention bias, did not train), with a replication on two held-out corpora under a pre-specified plan, an item-level Q-matrix ladder, authored KC structures (Junyi, DBE-KT22, XES3G5M KC routes), and simulated worlds with a known prerequisite graph used as a positive control and for next-KC decisions with prerequisite gating. Every run file, analysis output and script behind the tables and figures of the manuscript and its Online Resources is under kt/; unit tests in tests/.

Version 8.0.0 adds the runs and analyses of the fifth UMUAI version, the second revision (kt/src/r22_*.py, kt/runs_r22_sim, kt/runs_r22, kt/results_r22): 92 training runs (the null-graph ladder in a third simulated world in which learners often meet a KC before its prerequisites; partial perturbations of the Q-matrix), a two-dimensional IRT simulator and chance-corrected agreement within curriculum-restricted candidate sets for next-KC decisions, a closed loop with 24 tracers per world, a random policy, both oracles and intervals over training cells, and t-based power for every comparison. Earlier content (releases 2.0.0 to 7.0.0) is unchanged; version 7.0.0 was not released separately and is contained in this version.
